ns0:entry.ns0:title: feat(processor): add JointAffineProcessorStep (#5480)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(processor): add JointAffineProcessorStep (#5480)

LeRobot robots report joints in degrees and grippers from 0 to 100. A
policy trained on other units (radians, grippers from 0 to 1) or another
calibration needs those values mapped before normalization, and its
actions mapped back.

JointAffineProcessorStep maps the leading entries of the state and the
action with `scales * x + offsets`; `inverse=True` maps predicted actions
back to the robot. A negative scale flips a joint, and zero scales are
rejected. `transform_stats()` maps a dataset's stats the same way,
swapping min/max and the low/high quantiles on flipped joints, so a
normalizer placed after the step can use stats recorded in the robot's
units.

ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(datasets): import TorchCodec before the streaming worker threads start (#5484)

datasets looks twice in sys.modules for TorchCodec while it encodes a table. A decode thread that imported TorchCodec between the two lookups made Dataset.from_dict on a parquet thread raise UnboundLocalError, so streaming failed before the first batch.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: feat(fastwam): return the imagined video with return_predicted_video …
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(fastwam): return the imagined video with return_predicted_video (#5336)

* feat(fastwam): return the imagined video with return_predicted_video

FastWAM skips future-video generation at inference. With the opt-in
return_predicted_video, select_action also denoises the clip that follows
the current observation with the video expert alone and returns, with each
action, the imagined camera frames it moves toward (shown by --display_data),
following LingBot-VA's flag of the same name (#3757, #3923).

Video tokens never attend to action tokens, so the video-only pass gives the
same clip as infer_joint and leaves the actions unchanged; it also works for
Faster-WAM's shallow action experts, which the joint forward rejects.

* Trim comments and docs

* fix(fastwam): address review on predicted video

- select_action goes through predict_action_chunk again (torch.compile hook)
- video latents no longer consume the global RNG when the seed is None
- split cameras at the equal widths used when stacking them
- pass the predicted actions to action-conditioned video experts

ns0:entry.ns0:title: feat(policies): add the NAT VLA policy (nat_vla) (#5416)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(policies): add the NAT VLA policy (nat_vla) (#5416)

* feat(policies): add the NAT VLA policy (nat_vla)

A vision-language model (LFM2-VL) that writes NAT action tokens, fine-tunable with lerobot-train from the pretrained
ahad-j/nat-vla-450m.

- nat_tokenizer.py: the NAT action tokenizer, built from its own config and safetensors weights
  (ahad-j/nat-tokenizer-h32-l4-c6400 by default, swappable through --policy.action_tokenizer). It encodes and decodes
  actions of any number of columns, gives the tokens needed for a number of steps, the first tokens of a chunk that
  starts with given actions, and a streaming decoder that returns each latent's actions as its tokens arrive.
- modeling_nat_vla.py: the policy. Training is cross-entropy over the action tokens with the VLM's original token
  embeddings frozen. Inference generates the tokens greedily in a background thread and streams the chunk, so each
  latent's actions are returned as soon as its tokens are generated. With rtc_steps, the next chunk is generated
  while the current chunk's last actions run and starts with their tokens (token-prefix real-time chunking).
- configuration_nat_vla.py, processor_nat_vla.py: config and the default pre/post-processors (MIN_MAX actions).
- The VLM's architecture config, tokenizer and image processor come from the vlm/ subfolder of ahad-j/nat-vla-450m.
- Registration in the policy factory, the nat_vla extra, docs and tests.

* fix(nat_vla): address review

- Build the prompt token ids, image inputs and state bins in a NATVLATokenizerProcessorStep, saved with the
  checkpoint together with the VLM processor as vlm/; fine-tuning a checkpoint writes prompts with the active
  config's cameras, setup and control mode.
- Keep the VLM config in the policy config, so a checkpoint loads without config.vlm or the Hub.
- Start --policy.type=nat_vla from the pretrained weights in config.vlm.
- Leave train/eval mode to the caller.
- Follow config.dtype (bfloat16 by default); the NAT tokenizer always runs in float32.
- Pad with the tokenizer's pad id.
- Do not train the tokens of fully padded latents (action_is_pad).
- Support LeRobot real-time chunking (supports_rtc, predict_action_chunk(inference_delay,
  prev_chunk_left_over)): the chunk starts with the tokens of the actions that run during inference,
  rounded up to whole latents.
- Tests build a tiny LFM2-VL and NAT tokenizer instead of downloading the checkpoint.
- Apache license headers, policy README and a longer guide with evaluation and deployment commands.

* fix(nat_vla): address the second review

- Reject action normalization other than MIN_MAX: the NAT tokenizer encodes actions in [-1, 1].
- The processor left-pads the prompts and ends them with <action_start>, so training and generation append
  the action tokens with one torch.cat instead of unpadding and re-padding each prompt.
- Pin the Hub downloads with vlm_revision and action_tokenizer_revision.
- Tests build float32 policies: CPU bfloat16 kernels differ between processors.
- Docs: a note on the optional causal-conv1d kernels.

* fix(nat_vla): address the rest of the second review

- Model card note: the LFM Open License's commercial-use limit and redistribution terms.
- Copyright headers name Ahad Jawaid and The HuggingFace Inc. team.
- Docs: the LIBERO fine-tune command the evaluation uses, the recipe's steps and batch size with the GPU memory
  they need, and the rtc_steps values of the default tokenizer.
- Type annotations for the tokenizer's modules, the hooks and the processor step.
- uv.lock with the nat_vla extra.
- --policy.type keeps the NAT tokenizer of --policy.action_tokenizer instead of the one saved with the
  pretrained VLA.
